name: Curly Girly
summary: Curly Girly is an aesthetic marketed at young girls, heavily inspired by "diva" motifs, as well as 2000s celebrity and pop culture.
description: Curly Girly is an aesthetic marketed at young girls, heavily inspired by "diva" motifs, as well as 2000s celebrity and pop culture. The name is derived from the curled serif fonts and shapes used in this style, and is ornate, playful, and frilly. [ 1 ] Curly Girly may also be referred to as Libby Lu Kid [ 1 ] or Tween Diva. [ 2 ]
culturalContext: The term was coined by Jack Grimes, and foundational research was conducted by Evan Collins, both of the Consumer Aesthetics Research Institute. Curly Girly is primarily influenced by the Groovial aesthetic, mirroring its swirls, spirals, whirly patterns, and bold colors. Additional inspiration comes from the Whimsicraft aesthetic, which contributed to the 'down-to-earthiness' of Curly Girly. This aesthetic shares elements with many others that also originated in the 90s, including the broader design style Global Village Coffeehouse. Additionally, similar girly diva motifs are present in Shoe Diva, although more "grown up" in comparison to the child-oriented Curly Girly.
